responseReviews.1: Replaced six paragraphs of generic framing with an account of divided will from Confessions VIII; distinguished ignorance, compulsion and conflicting attachments. Retained the historical-setting/contribution/influence order and all five list slots; qualified invention-of-introspection claims.
responseReviews.2: Developed the four concepts with memory retrieval, remembered sorrow and temporal recitation. Preserved concept order and effective memory/divided-love formulations. Distinguished desire from proof of its ultimate object, temporal awareness from the unreality of physical time, and introspection from modern scientific theory.
responseReviews.3: Retained the skeptical challenge to premature theological explanation; explained the inferential gap, a charitable wider-case reply, grace as enabling rather than coercing, and the residual responsibility objection. Added an explicitly hypothetical promise-breaking example and kept all five objection/reply/test list positions.
responseReviews.4: Replaced generic reading advice with Confessions VIII/X/XI and a comparison of distinct works On Free Choice of the Will and On Grace and Free Will. Preserved the five list positions and original central question about knowing better but choosing worse.

supplementalReferences.work: Cambridge University Press edition: distinguishes the early and later works on will and grace
